private.finalText:
I've written the hidden suite in `test/hidden-pathe-basename-trailing-confirmed/`, split into `basename.spec.ts` (18 tests) and `parse.spec.ts` (13 tests). `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors. I copied the repo to the scratchpad and added a correct `basename` there (keep the last non-empty segment); all 31 hidden tests and all 38 public tests pass against it.

**The seam isn't stubbed.** `src/path.ts` still contains the old `basename`/`parse` bodies; only doc comments were added. They don't throw `not implemented`. So against the seam as it stands, 23 tests fail and 8 pass. Those 8 cover scenarios where the spec keeps the old result, so no test can fail there without asserting a different scenario:
- `[happy-1]`, `[happy-7]`, `[boundary-12]`: the spec says these results stay the same.
- `[boundary-4]`, `[boundary-5]`, `[boundary-9]`, and both `[boundary-11]` tests: every expected value is `""`, which the old code already returns.

The public suite has the same limit for these scenarios.

**Shortcuts I checked.** I ran both suites against shortcut implementations:
- **Pop up to 5 trailing empty segments:** passes the whole public suite. The hidden tests catch it with runs of 10–50 separators.
- **Strip trailing separators from the extension:** caught by the extension tests ending in `\` or a mixed separator.
- **Trim whitespace from segments:** passes the public suite. The test with `"/temp /"` catches it.

Each hidden test names the public test it extends in a comment. Other cases that only the hidden suite covers: 200-segment paths, other drive letters, extensions that reach into the parent folder, `"C:/"` with extension `"C:"`, and `parse` checked against `basename`/`extname`/`dirname`. Nothing was written outside the hidden test folder.

31 tests, in 2 files.

Open in the spec: none
